title: Cerebras raises $5.5B in comeback IPO
caption: Cerebras just pulled off a $5.5B IPO after nearly dying last year. The chip maker's comeback shows why hardware timing matters more than technology. Link in bio for the full story.

slides.headline: Cerebras nearly died. Then raised $5.5B
slides.sub: The chip maker everyone wrote off just kicked off 2026's IPO season

slides.body: A year ago Cerebras was scrambling for bridge funding. Today they opened at $42 per share, pricing above range. Wall Street is betting big on AI chips that aren't Nvidia.

slides.title: Build wafer-scale chips
slides.body: Cerebras makes chips the size of dinner plates. One wafer holds 850,000 cores vs Nvidia's 80. The physics shouldn't work but somehow does. They ship to 14 countries now.

slides.title: Survive the trough
slides.body: Mid-2025 their biggest customer went dark. Burn rate hit $60M per quarter. Founders took zero salary for 8 months. Three board members quit. The pivot to inference chips saved them.

slides.title: Timing beat technology
bullets: Nvidia lead times hit 11 months in Q1 2026
Inference costs became the new bottleneck
Enterprises want chip diversity for leverage
slides.footer: The market opened because Nvidia couldn't ship fast enough

slides.title: What this signals
slides.body: First major AI hardware IPO since the GPU shortage began. If Cerebras holds above $40, expect Groq and SambaNova to file by Q3. The AI infrastructure layer is finally liquid.

slides.hook: Hardware timing matters more than specs
